inputs.coverage: all 302 ids ruled on by all three judges; zero uncovered ids

reconciliation_policy: ACCEPT if >=2 of 3 judges vote keep (majority keep).
KILL if not accepted and >=2 of 3 judges vote kill (majority kill).

MERGE otherwise (majority or plurality merge); merge target = majority target among proposing judges; ties broken in favor of Judge A (dedup specialist); targets validated to land in the accepted set, following chains if needed (none were needed).

The single 3-way split W13-P1-C-041 (A:merge, B:kill, C:keep) resolved as MERGE into W13-P1-C-021: majority is not-keep, and merge preserves the content inside an accepted program rather than discarding it against one judge's keep.

tie_breaks.note: A proposed C-066, C proposed C-068, B voted kill; C-068 is itself merged (not accepted), so only C-066 is a valid terminal; also Judge A dedup preference.
A proposed C-023, C proposed C-086 (both accepted); tie broken in favor of dedup-specialist Judge A; alternate target C-086 recorded here.

reasons.A: Permutation kill: early-exit/dynamic-depth ported to SAM; efficiency framing with thin scientific content beyond established early-exit literature (prior-art risk HYPOTHESIS, unverified).
reasons.B: Efficiency recipe wearing a hypothesis costume: 'easy prompts saturate at shallower depth' is near-certain, and confirming it yields a router paper rather than a falsified belief. Architecture-permutation (early-exit ported to SAM).
reasons.C: Early-exit / dynamic-depth is a mature efficiency literature ported to SAM. No belief challenged; the mechanism ('easy inputs saturate early') is the premise of that literature, not a finding. Unverified prior-art risk: very high.

reasons.A: Permutation kill: curriculum-ordering ported to sequential adapters; classic curriculum-effect template, compute-heavy (flagged by generator itself), low distinctiveness.
reasons.B: Curriculum-order effect for sequential adapters is noise-dominated: settling it honestly needs many seeds x orders x domains, expensive relative to a generic payoff. Permutation of curriculum learning onto adapters.
reasons.C: Curriculum/ordering is a generic continual-learning permutation (orders x domains). Mechanism stated at metaphor level ('breaks structures'); falsification requires a combinatorial sweep of sequential adaptations. High cost, low distinctiveness.

reasons.A: Prior-art-risk kill (HYPOTHESIS, unverified): mIoU-vs-boundary-quality divergence is a well-trodden metric critique with established boundary-quality metrics; no distinct new hypothesis beyond them.
reasons.B: Boundary-vs-region metric divergence is established practice (boundary-quality metrics exist for exactly this reason); residual novelty (human editing-utility link) is a user study bolted onto a known result.
reasons.C: Strawman community belief: the field demonstrably does not hold that region overlap suffices; boundary-quality metrics are standard practice. The contrarian frame is manufactured; what remains is a correlation audit.

reasons.A: Prior-art-risk kill (HYPOTHESIS, unverified): attention-map faithfulness failure is a heavily studied critique (attention-vs-occlusion faithfulness); port to current ViT checkpoints adds little hypothesis content.
reasons.B: Attention-faithfulness failure is a heavily published area; the proposed occlusion-agreement test replicates known designs. Killed as redundant, not infeasible.
reasons.C: Attention-vs-explanation faithfulness is a famous, extensively litigated debate. The idea restates it for vision transformers without a new falsifiable twist.

reasons.A: Permutation kill: direct port of the known emergence-is-a-metric-artifact critique to vision benchmarks; hypothesis is not new, only the substrate (prior-art risk HYPOTHESIS, unverified).
reasons.B: Direct port of the famous emergence-is-a-metric-artifact result to vision benchmarks; permutation with high prior-art risk and no new falsification design.
reasons.C: The metric-artifact account of emergent abilities is a widely known position; porting it to visual tasks changes neither the hypothesis nor the test.

reasons.A: Prior-art-risk kill (HYPOTHESIS, unverified): non-transfer of adversarial robustness across threat models is repeatedly documented; the proposed matrix is an audit of a known result.

reasons.C: Non-transfer of adversarial robustness across threat models is a well-documented negative result. The proposed cross-threat matrix is a replication catalog, not a new claim.
